chapters.1.lds: The lesson connects considering one’s ways with giving temple work higher priority. Why does Haggai compare private houses with God’s ruined house?
chapters.1.summary: In the second year of Darius, Haggai speaks to the governor and the high priest. The people say it is not yet time to rebuild the LORD’s house. God asks whether they should live in paneled houses while his house lies ruined. They sow much and harvest little. Their wages go into a bag with holes. God tells them to bring wood and build. The leaders and the people obey. Within a month the work begins.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson compares encouragement for the builders with later Church teaching about temples. Why does the promise of presence matter before greater glory or a new harvest?
chapters.2.summary: A month later Haggai speaks again. He asks who remembers the first temple in its glory. The new one looks like nothing beside it. Yet God tells the governor, the priest, and the people to be strong and work. He is with them, and his Spirit remains among them. He will shake the nations and fill this house with glory. From the day the foundation was laid, he will bless them. He tells the governor that he has chosen him.
